methodology.title: How we calculate
methodology.metaDescription: Observatório Habitação's calculations explained: the four scenarios, the metrics, taxes, costs, financing, data sources and assumptions.
methodology.intro: Observatório Habitação applies costs, Portuguese taxes and financing to the market values you enter, and compares four strategies. This page explains how, in plain language.
methodology.scenariosIntro: All scenarios start from the same property data. The purchase happens in month 0 and the calculation runs month by month until the sale or the assignment.
methodology.scenarioFlip: Buy, renovate during the months you set and sell at the price after renovation. While you hold the property you pay IMI, condominium, insurance, utilities and loan payments. On the sale you pay the agency commission (with VAT), repay the loan and pay capital gains tax.
methodology.scenarioLongTerm: The property is let for good, without a sale. Rent starts after the renovation and leases follow one another, each as long as you set, separated by the months of vacancy between leases; rent rises every year (by default, the latest legal update coefficient). Operating costs (IMI, condominium, insurance, maintenance and management) are deducted from the rent for income tax; loan interest is not. Profit and IRR are worked out over 30 years (or the loan term, if longer).
methodology.scenarioShortTerm: For each month: booked nights = days × the season's occupancy; stays = nights ÷ average stay. Revenue includes the nights and the cleaning fees. You pay platform commissions, management, cleaning, consumables and utilities. Income tax follows the simplified regime (category B).
methodology.scenarioCessao: You pay the deposit when signing the CPCV and, before the deed, assign your position to another buyer. You receive the assignment price (which includes the deposit reimbursement), pay commission on the premium and other costs, and pay tax on the gain.
methodology.metricsIntro: The same metrics for every scenario, so you can compare them.
methodology.acquisitionImt: IMT (transfer tax): on the higher of the price and the tax value (VPT), using the table for the property's use (own permanent home or other housing); a flat rate for other urban property (6.5%) and rustic property (5%).
methodology.acquisitionNonResident: Non-resident buyers: since 20 May 2026, housing bought by non-residents pays a flat 7.5% IMT, refunded if the buyer becomes resident in Portugal within 2 years or lets at a capped rent.
methodology.acquisitionStamp: Stamp duty: 0.8% on the purchase, 0.6% on the loan and 4% on the interest paid to the bank.
methodology.acquisitionFees: Casa Pronta (deed and registration): €375, or €700 with a mortgage. Valuation (€250) and process opening (€300): typical values, which you can change.
methodology.financingText: By default the purchase is paid with your own money, without a loan. With a loan: a fixed instalment at the TAEG you enter, used as the global interest rate; 30 years by default, up to 50. Stamp duty on the loan (0.6%), the property valuation, the process opening fee and the mortgage registration (Casa Pronta with mortgage) are paid separately at purchase. The default amount is the most banks lend: 90% for your own permanent home, 80% for other purposes (Banco de Portugal limits). On a sale, the outstanding balance is repaid with a 0.5% early repayment fee.
methodology.taxesRental: Rent (category F): a flat 25% rate, reduced to 15%, 10% or 5% for leases of 5, 10 or 20 years; or aggregated with your other income and taxed at the IRS brackets.
methodology.taxesAl: Short-term rental (category B, simplified regime): 35% of revenue (50% in containment zones) is added to your other income and taxed at the IRS brackets. 6% VAT only applies if you are registered; we warn you when revenue exceeds the 15 000 € exemption threshold.
methodology.taxesGains: Capital gains: there is no fixed rate. 50% of the gain is added to your other taxable income and taxed at the IRS brackets (12.5% to 48% in 2026, plus the solidarity surcharge above 80 000 €), for residents and non-residents alike. The gain is the sale price minus the selling commission, the purchase price, IMT, stamp duty, deed costs and renovation.
methodology.taxesCessao: Contract assignment: 50% of the gain is added to your other income and taxed at the IRS brackets (CIRS art. 43 with art. 10 no. 1 d)). If the CPCV allows assignment to a third party, IMT and stamp duty may be due when it is signed: you can include them.
methodology.exitTitle: Sale at the end of the period
methodology.exitText: For short-term rental, the property is sold at the end of the holding period at today's value, with no appreciation: the value after renovation (if you renovate) or the market value. The sale counts in profit, ROI and IRR, but not in payback. Long-term rental has no sale.
methodology.dataIne: Prices and rents: INE medians by municipality and parish (sale price per m² over 12 months, quarterly; rent per m² of new leases, yearly). District figures are the median of the municipalities' medians, calculated by Observatório Habitação.
methodology.dataCaop: Administrative boundaries: CAOP 2025 from Direção-Geral do Território (CC BY 4.0), used to find the parish of an address.
methodology.dataEuribor: Euribor: monthly averages published by the European Central Bank.
methodology.dataImi: IMI rates: an open transcription (CC BY 4.0) of the rates published by the tax authority, still to be checked against the official source. Some municipalities set rates per parish and are not included.
methodology.dataTax: Tax parameters: stored by year and version, from the tax codes published on Portal das Finanças. Not yet reviewed by an accountant.
methodology.assumptionsText: You can change all of these under “Assumptions”.
assumptionsList: Condominium and insurance per deal: resale and AL 50 €/month and 250 €/year; rental 25 €/month and home insurance 20 €/month
Selling commission 5% + VAT; no property appreciation
Long-term rental: consecutive leases with 1 month vacant between them, yearly increase by the latest rent update coefficient (2.24% for 2026), maintenance 10% of rent, no management

Short-term rental: platform commission 15%, management 20%, maintenance 20% of revenue, average stay 3 nights, cleaning fee charged 40 € and paid 35 €, consumables 4 €/night, utilities 150 €/month, furniture 10 000 €, registration 1 000 €
Contract assignment: 5% + VAT commission on the premium, 1 000 € other costs, 6 months to the assignment
No other income unless you enter your taxable income; resale 12 months after purchase; AL for 10 years; long-term rental kept for good, analysed over 30 years
Opportunity signal: asking price more than 5% below the market value you entered
simplificationsList: Rental income tax is paid once per 12-month period; capital gains tax is paid in the month of the sale (in reality, the following year).
IMI is spread over the months (in reality, it is paid by whoever owns the property on 31 December).
Rental losses are not carried forward to later years.
If you do not know the VPT, we use the purchase price, which may overstate IMI.
The loan only finances the purchase and is drawn in full in month 0.
methodology.notModelledTitle: What we do not calculate yet
notModelledList: The young buyers' IMT table and the IMT Jovem and own-home reinvestment exemptions
Inflation correction coefficients for property held more than 24 months
Adicional ao IMI, social security contributions and purchases through a company
Capital gains on property used for short-term rental (category B rules)
Checking short-term rental registrations and containment zones (comes with the national AL registry)

faq.q: Why do I have to enter the market value and the rent?
faq.a: In this first version, Observatório Habitação does not estimate these values automatically. We show the area's INE medians as a reference; individual properties can differ a lot.

faq.q: Do the results replace an accountant?
faq.a: No. They are estimates to compare strategies. Before deciding, check taxes and costs with an accountant or lawyer.
The most recent active parameter set. The year is shown below the results.

faq.q: Why can't I read links from some sites?
faq.a: We only read listings from sites whose terms of use allow it. You can always fill in the details yourself.

faq.q: How do I save or share a scenario?
faq.a: Sign in with your email (no password) and use “Save”. Saved scenarios are under “Account”.

faq.q: I found a mistake. How do I report it?
faq.a: Use the contacts page. Include the scenario link or the values you entered, so we can reproduce the calculation.

metrics.totalInvestmentHelp: Purchase price plus acquisition costs, renovation, furnishing and licences.
metrics.ownCapitalHelp: The money you put in yourself: total investment minus the loan.
metrics.peakCapitalHelp: The most you have invested at any point, including costs while the property earns nothing.
metrics.netProfitHelp: Everything you receive minus everything you pay, including the final sale, after taxes and the loan.
metrics.roiHelp: Return on own capital: net profit divided by the own capital invested.
metrics.irrHelp: Internal rate of return: the equivalent annual return, taking into account when each euro goes in and out.
metrics.grossYieldHelp: Annual rent divided by the purchase price plus acquisition costs.
metrics.netYieldHelp: Annual rent minus operating costs and taxes, divided by the total investment. Excludes the loan.
metrics.monthlyCashFlowHelp: What is left (or missing) each month in the first full year, after costs, taxes and loan payments.
metrics.paybackYearsHelp: Years until cash flow pays back your own capital, not counting the sale.
metrics.returnOnDepositHelp: Net profit of the assignment divided by the deposit paid on the CPCV.
metrics.acquisitionCostsHelp: Paid at purchase: IMT, stamp duty on the purchase, Casa Pronta (deed and registration) and, with a loan, stamp duty on the loan, valuation and process opening.
metrics.annualCashFlowHelp: What is left each year after costs, taxes and loan payments: the monthly cash flow × 12.
metrics.lifetimeCashFlowHelp: Rent minus costs, taxes and loan payments over the whole period (for a rental kept for good, 30 years or the loan term), without the purchase or a sale.
metrics.cashOnCashHelp: Annual cash flow ÷ own capital invested: what the money you put in earns each year.

gainTax.title: IRS on the capital gain
gainTax.help: When you sell at a gain, you pay IRS on the capital gain (category G). The gain is what the sale brings in minus what the property cost you (price, IMT, stamp duty, deed and works) and the selling commission. It is paid with the following year's IRS return; here it counts in the month of the sale.

lines.upfrontTaxes: IMT and stamp duty paid at the CPCV

gainTax.noGain: No gain at this price: no IRS on the capital gain.
gainTax.explain: Only {share} of the gain ({taxable}) is taxed: it is added to your other taxable income ({other}) and pays IRS at the brackets it falls in: {rates}.
gainTax.notDeducted: IMI, condominium, insurance and interest are not deducted from the gain: that is why you can pay this tax even when the deal barely makes a profit.
gainTax.otherZero: Your other taxable income counts as €0 (the field is blank or zero), so the gain starts in the lowest bracket. If you have a salary or pension, enter your annual taxable income under taxes: the gain falls in higher brackets and the tax goes up.
gainTax.chartNote: Gains IRS: {tax}. Selling for {price}, the gain is {gain} (sale minus commission, price, IMT, stamp duty, deed and works; IMI, condominium, insurance and interest are not deducted). Only {share} of it, {taxable}, is taxed: {rates}.
gainTax.chartOtherZero: Other taxable income blank or zero: with a salary or pension, the rate would be higher.

warnings.ltv_above_limit: The loan exceeds Banco de Portugal's recommended limit (80% for investment, 90% for your own home).
warnings.holding_shorter_than_renovation: The holding period is shorter than the renovation.
warnings.negative_cash_flow: Monthly cash flow is negative: you will need to cover the difference every month.
warnings.al_containment_zone: Short-term rental containment zone: new registrations may be restricted.
warnings.al_registrations_suspended: New short-term rental registrations are suspended in this area.
warnings.al_status_unknown: We could not confirm whether new short-term rental registrations are allowed.
warnings.al_vat_threshold_exceeded: Annual turnover is above the VAT exemption threshold (15 000 €). Consider charging VAT.
warnings.assignment_above_market: The buyer of the position would pay more than the market value you entered.
warnings.assignment_upfront_imt: With an assignment clause in the CPCV, IMT and stamp duty may be due when it is signed.
warnings.imt_non_resident: Non-resident buyer: flat 7.5% IMT (since 20/05/2026). The difference is refunded if you become resident in Portugal within 2 years, or let at a capped rent within 6 months for at least 36 of the first 60 months.

evaluate.intro: Paste a listing link or enter the details by hand, choose the kind of deal and see the numbers: costs, taxes, financing and returns.
evaluate.linkHelp: Paste the link and our AI reads the listing for you. We only read listings from sites that allow it.
evaluate.linkRead: Details read from the listing. Check them and fill in anything missing.
evaluate.linkNotAllowed: This site does not allow listings to be read automatically. Please fill in the details.

evaluate.rateLimited: Too many requests in a row. Wait a few minutes and try again.
evaluate.marketReferenceHelp: INE medians for the property's area. They are a reference: individual properties vary.
evaluate.noReference: No market data for this area.
evaluate.chooseArea: Choose the location to see local prices.
evaluate.marketValueHelp: What the property is worth today, as it is.
evaluate.resaleValueHelp: What you expect to sell for after renovating (resale scenario).
evaluate.nightlyRatesHelp: Average price charged per night in each season, VAT included where applicable.
evaluate.occupancyRatesHelp: Share of nights booked in each season.
evaluate.cpcvPriceHelp: Price agreed in the promissory purchase contract (CPCV).
evaluate.depositHelp: Amount paid when the CPCV was signed (sinal).
evaluate.assignmentPriceHelp: Total the new buyer pays you for the position, including the deposit reimbursement.
evaluate.upfrontTransferTaxes: CPCV allows assignment to a third party
evaluate.upfrontTransferTaxesHelp: If the contract allows the position to be assigned, IMT and stamp duty may be due on signing.

opportunity.text: Asking price {diff} vs. the market value you entered.

evaluate.loanAmountHelp: By default, the most banks lend for the chosen use (Banco de Portugal limits). You can enter another amount.
evaluate.interestRateHelp: The TAEG is used as the loan's global interest rate: it sets the monthly instalment. Stamp duty on the loan (0.6% of the amount), the process opening fee and the property valuation are added separately at purchase and are not included in this rate. Use the TAEG from the bank's offer; by default we use 12-month Euribor ({euribor}) + a typical spread ({spread}).
evaluate.interestRateHelpNoEuribor: The TAEG is used as the loan's global interest rate: it sets the monthly instalment. Stamp duty on the loan (0.6% of the amount), the process opening fee and the property valuation are added separately at purchase and are not included in this rate.
evaluate.contractYearsHelp: Leases follow one another, each this long, separated only by the vacancy between leases set in the assumptions. With the flat rate, leases of 5, 10 or 20 years pay reduced income tax.
evaluate.assumptionsHelp: Reasonable defaults. Adjust them to your case.
evaluate.vptHelp: Shown on the caderneta predial. Leave blank if unknown.
evaluate.sellingCommission: Agency commission on the sale (excl. VAT)
evaluate.sellingCommissionHelp: The share of the sale price the estate agency charges, excluding VAT (23% VAT is added in the calculation). In Portugal 3% to 5% is usual, often negotiable. Enter 0 if you sell without an agency.
evaluate.commissionHint: = {amount} with VAT, on a sale for {price}
evaluate.vacancyHelp: Months without a tenant between the end of one lease and the start of the next.
evaluate.assignmentCommissionHelp: The share of the premium (assignment price minus the deposit) the agency charges, excluding VAT (23% VAT is added in the calculation). Enter 0 if there is no agency.

missingFields.cessao: CPCV price, deposit and assignment price

evaluate.parameters: {year} tax parameters (pending review by an accountant).
evaluate.noParameters: No active tax parameters. Calculations are unavailable.
evaluate.signinToSave: To save, you need to sign in. The evaluation stays in this browser and is saved to your account as soon as you sign in.
evaluate.limitReached: You have reached your plan's limit of saved scenarios.
evaluate.saveError: Could not save. Please try again.
evaluate.buyerNonResidentHelp: Since 20 May 2026, housing bought by non-residents pays a flat 7.5% IMT, refundable under certain conditions.
evaluate.readingHelp: Reading the listing… this can take a few seconds.
evaluate.linkNotListing: This page does not look like a listing of a property for sale.
evaluate.manualIntro: Check or enter the property details.
evaluate.mapsUrlHelp: In Google Maps, open the place, tap “Share” and paste the link here. When a listing is read, its location is used.
evaluate.mapsUrlInvalid: This is not a Google Maps link (for example, https://maps.app.goo.gl/…).
evaluate.dealQuestion: Which deals do you want to evaluate? You can choose several and compare them.

dealIntro.flip: Enter what you expect to sell the property for and how long until the sale.
dealIntro.longTermRental: Enter the rent you expect and the length of each lease. The market value is optional: it is compared with the asking price.
dealIntro.shortTermRental: Enter the nightly rate and occupancy for each season, and what the property is worth today.

evaluate.holdingYearsHelp: How many years you keep the property before selling it. The sale is taken at today's value, with no appreciation.
evaluate.nightlyGrowth: Yearly increase of the nightly rate
evaluate.compareHelp: The four strategies side by side, with the indicators of each.
evaluate.dealsChosen: {count} deals chosen: you will fill in the details of each, in turn.
evaluate.ltvInfo: For this use, banks lend up to {ltv} of the value (minimum down payment {down}).
evaluate.otherTaxableIncomeHelp: Your annual taxable income from other sources (salaries, pensions…). Sale gains (50% of the gain), short-term rental income and rents you choose to aggregate are added to it and taxed at the IRS brackets. Left empty, it counts as zero.
evaluate.irsBracketsHint: IRS worked out with the {year} brackets ({min} to {max}).
evaluate.englobamentoNote: With taxable income up to {income} (marginal rate up to {marginal}), adding rents to your income can cost less IRS than the {flat} flat rate. Above that, the flat rate is usually better.
evaluate.rentGrowthHelp: By default, the rent update coefficient for {year} ({rate}), the latest set by law: {source}, published in the Diário da República from INE's price index. Landlords may raise the rent once a year up to this amount.
evaluate.rentGrowthHelpNoSource: Yearly rent increase. The legal limit is the rent update coefficient published every year in the Diário da República.
evaluate.permanentRentalNote: The property is let for good, without a sale. Results show the monthly, annual and lifetime cash flow over {years} years.
evaluate.permanentRentalResults: Let for good, without a sale: lifetime cash flow over {years} years; no sale profit or IRR.
evaluate.loanTermHelp: {recommended} years by default: the longest term Banco de Portugal recommends for a new mortgage (macroprudential measure). You can enter up to {max} years if your bank accepts it.
evaluate.loanTermAboveRecommended: Above the {recommended} years Banco de Portugal recommends: few banks accept it.
evaluate.loanFeesHelp: Fees the bank charges when the loan is signed. Typical 2026 values: valuation €190–320, process opening €135–320. Check your bank's price list or offer.
evaluate.annualCostsHelp: Recurring costs of owning the property in a typical year, already deducted from the cash flow: IMI (VPT, or the price if unknown, × the municipal rate), condominium, home insurance and maintenance (10% of the rent for a long-term rental, 20% of revenue for AL, by default).
evaluate.holdingCosts: Costs until the sale ({months, plural, one {1 month} other {# months}})
evaluate.holdingCostsHelp: What owning the property costs until it is sold, counted only for the months until the sale (as in the calculation): IMI, condominium and home insurance.

prices.title: House prices in Portugal
prices.intro: Median sale price and rent per m², by district, municipality and parish.
prices.areaIntro: Median sale price and rent per m² in {area}.
prices.grossYieldHelp: Median annual rent divided by the median sale price. Indicative: excludes costs and taxes.
prices.metaDescription: Median sale price and rent per m² in {area}: trends, gross yield and comparison with neighbouring areas.
prices.fallbackNote: No figures of its own for this area: showing the values for {area}.
prices.derivedNote: INE does not publish district figures. District values are the median of its municipalities' medians, calculated by Observatório Habitação from INE data.
prices.overviewNote: Districts: median of the municipalities' medians (calculated by Observatório Habitação from INE data). Açores and Madeira: figures published by INE.

sell.title: What is your home worth?
sell.intro: Describe the property and see its likely value, a range and an asking price, based on INE's medians for the parish and on similar listings. With the sale's details, also see what you keep after the commission, IRS and the loan.
sell.locationHelp: INE's median sale price for the parish is the base of the valuation.
sell.areaHelp: Usable area, as in the property record or the energy certificate.
sell.conditionHelp: INE's median stands for a used property. New: +15 %; to recover: −25 % (assumptions).
sell.featuresHelp: Extras are not added to the price: a property without one of these is worth less. No lift from the 2nd floor: −5 % a floor (up to −15 %); no garage: −5 %; no balcony: −3 %.
sell.comparablesIntro: Optional but recommended: add listings of similar properties in the same area. With 3 or more they count towards the value (50 %; 70 % with 5 or more). Give each one's floor and what it lacks: a listing without a lift or garage is adjusted before it is compared.
sell.saleIntro: Optional: to see what you keep. Leave blank whatever you don't know.
sell.commissionHelp: Percentage of the price, excluding VAT (23 % VAT is added). Usual: 3 % to 5 %. Enter 0 if selling without an agency.
sell.otherSaleCostsHelp: For example the energy certificate, required to sell.
sell.purchaseGroupHelp: To work out the IRS on the gain.
sell.purchasePriceHelp: The price in the purchase deed (or the tax value used for IMT, if higher).
sell.purchaseYearHelp: After 24 months, the purchase price is corrected for inflation (coeficientes de desvalorização da moeda). Bought before 1989: the gain pays no IRS.
sell.purchaseCostsHelp: What you paid when buying. Deducted from the gain.
sell.worksHelp: Improvement works of the last 12 years, with invoices. Deducted from the gain.
sell.ownHome: It is my own permanent home
sell.ownHomeHelp: If you reinvest in another own permanent home (24 months before or 36 months after the sale), the gain pays no IRS in proportion to the amount reinvested.
sell.reinvestmentHelp: Measured against the sale price less the loan repaid with the sale. Reinvesting all of it, the gain pays no IRS.
sell.loanBalanceHelp: The capital still owed, repaid with the sale.
sell.earlyRepaymentHelp: On the capital repaid. Legal maximum: 0.5 % with a variable rate, 2 % with a fixed rate. Check with your bank.
sell.otherIncome: Other taxable income in the year
sell.otherIncomeHelp: Half the gain is added to your other income and taxed by the IRS brackets. Blank: the gain alone, in the lowest bracket.

confidenceText.low: Based mostly on INE's median for the area: this property's value may differ a lot. Add 3 or more similar listings for a more reliable estimate.
confidenceText.medium: INE's median and a few similar listings. With 5 or more listings, the estimate gets tighter.
confidenceText.high: INE's median and at least 5 similar listings.

sell.askingPriceHelp: The likely value plus a 5 % margin to negotiate: buyers almost always make a counter-offer.
sell.listingsAskingSub: median of {count, plural, one {1 listing} other {# listings}}
sell.adviceMargin: A price set too high keeps buyers away and the property on the market for longer; review it if there are no viewings in the first weeks.
sell.adviceTrend: In {area}, INE's median changed {change} in a year.
sell.adviceListings: The suggested price per m² is {diff} against what similar listings ask.
sell.howNoIne: No INE median for this area
sell.howBase: Standard property (used, with lift, garage and balcony)
sell.howListingsNote: Each listing: asking price less a {margin} negotiation margin, divided by its own adjustment (condition and what it lacks), to compare it with a standard property. What a listing does not say is taken as the same as this property.
sell.howAssumptions: The adjustments and margins are assumptions (model {version}), to review with real sales data. INE's median refers to transaction prices, not asking prices.
sell.proceedsPrompt: Enter the sale and purchase details to see the amount after the commission, IRS and the loan.
sell.netIrsHint: Enter the purchase price to work out the IRS on the gain.
sell.gainUntaxed: Bought before 1989: the gain pays no IRS.

privacy.intro: This policy explains what personal data Observatório Habitação collects, what it is used for, how long it is kept and how you can exercise your rights, under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR, Regulation (EU) 2016/679) and Portuguese Law 58/2019.

sections.title: Who is responsible for your data
paragraphs: The controller is [entity name], tax number [number], registered at [address]. For any question about your data, write to [contact email].

sections.title: What data we collect
items: Account: your email (to sign in with a link, without a password) and your name.
Profile, if you wish: phone and date of birth.
What you save: scenarios, sale valuations, photos you upload, listing links you analyse and your account settings.
Contact requests: the name, email, phone and message you send us.
Technical data: the session cookie, your IP address (to limit abuse, such as repeated sign-in link requests) and server logs.
If you sign in with Google: the name, email and profile picture Google shares with us.
paragraphs: We don't ask for sensitive data (such as health, religion or ethnic origin). You don't need an account to use the calculators.

sections.title: What we use the data for, and on what basis
paragraphs: We don't sell your data or use it for third-party advertising. We make no automated decisions with legal effects on you: the site's estimates are calculations you ask for.

sections.title: Who we share it with
paragraphs: We use service providers (processors) who handle data only on our behalf and on our instructions:
items: Hosting of the site and database: [hosting provider].
Sending emails (sign-in links and reports): Resend.
Sign-in with Google, if you choose it: Google.
after: We only share data with partners (mortgage, lawyers, surveys) when you ask us to. We may also have to disclose it to authorities when the law requires.

sections.title: Transfers outside the EU
paragraphs: Some providers may process data outside the European Economic Area (for example, in the United States). In those cases the transfer relies on GDPR safeguards: a European Commission adequacy decision (such as the EU-US Data Privacy Framework) or standard contractual clauses.

sections.title: How long we keep data
items: Account, profile, scenarios, valuations and photos: while you have an account. When you delete it, they are deleted.
Phone and date of birth: until you delete them in your account, or delete the account.
Contact requests: as long as needed to follow them up. If you delete your account, they are anonymised.
Listing analyses: when you delete your account, they are no longer linked to you.
Session: 5 days. Sign-in links: 1 hour. Rate-limit records: 1 hour.
Backups: replaced after about two weeks.
Data the law requires us to keep: for the legal period.

sections.title: Your rights
paragraphs: You have the right to access, correct and delete your data, to restrict or object to its processing, to receive it in a portable format and to withdraw consent at any time, without affecting processing done before.

In your account you can, without contacting us, change your name, phone and date of birth, manage your consents, download all your data and delete the account. For anything else, write to [contact email]: we reply within one month.
If you think we are not handling your data properly, you can complain to the Portuguese data protection authority (CNPD, www.cnpd.pt).

sections.title: Minimum age
paragraphs: Accounts are for people aged 16 or over. If you know that someone under 16 has created an account, tell us so we can delete it.

sections.title: Security
paragraphs: You sign in without a password, with single-use links valid for 1 hour. Connections to the site are encrypted (HTTPS), access to the database is restricted and repeated requests are limited. No system is infallible: if a data breach affects you, we will tell you and the CNPD, as the law requires.

sections.title: Cookies
paragraphs: We only use essential cookies: the session (when you sign in), language and theme. We use no analytics or advertising cookies.

sections.title: Changes to this policy
paragraphs: If we change this policy, we update the date at the top. If the change is significant, we will let you know by email.
